questions.domain: Describe an analytics workload on Azure
questions.topic: MPP Table Distribution in Dedicated SQL Pools (Hash, Round-Robin, Replicated)
questions.stem: In a massively parallel processing (MPP) architecture such as an Azure Synapse Analytics Dedicated SQL pool, data is spread across 60 underlying distributions. An architect wants to optimize the storage of two tables: a massive fact table (FactInternetSales containing 500 million rows) and a small dimension table (DimCurrency containing 150 rows) to eliminate expensive Data Movement (Shuffle) operations during JOIN queries. Which distribution strategy does Microsoft recommend for each table?

options.text: Hash distribution for the large fact table (FactInternetSales) and Replicated distribution (full copy on each node) for the small dimension table (DimCurrency).
options.rationale: Correct. Distributing large fact tables by a deterministic Hash key and replicating (Replicated) small dimension tables (< 2 GB) across all compute nodes allows JOINs to resolve locally without moving data across the network.

options.text: Replicated distribution across all nodes for the 500 million row fact table and Hash distribution for the temporary staging table.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Replicating a massive fact table would multiply its storage requirements by the number of compute nodes, causing extreme storage overhead.

options.text: Round-Robin distribution for both the large fact table and the dimension table to completely avoid configuring join keys in SQL queries.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Using Round-Robin for both tables forces the MPP engine to shuffle rows across the network during every JOIN operation.

options.text: External Azure Queue Storage message queues of 64 KB to eliminate partitioning tables across the 60 underlying pool distributions.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Azure Queue Storage is an asynchronous messaging service, not a distributed table design strategy in a Synapse Dedicated SQL pool.

questions.explanation: In an MPP engine like Azure Synapse Dedicated SQL Pool, a Control Node coordinates queries across multiple Compute Nodes connected to 60 distributions. Three table distribution options exist: 1) Hash (distributes rows deterministically based on a single hash key column, ideal for large fact tables > 2 GB); 2) Replicated (stores a complete copy of the table on each compute node, ideal for small dimension tables < 2 GB to eliminate network shuffle during JOINs); and 3) Round-Robin (distributes rows evenly and randomly, default option, ideal for temporary staging tables).

theoryPill.title: Distribution Strategies in MPP Engines: Hash, Replicated, and Round-Robin
theoryPill.summary: Understanding when to apply Hash, Replicated, and Round-Robin distributions is a classic question in Microsoft Azure data exams.
keyPoints: Hash-distributed: Distributes rows using a hash function on a key column; ideal for large fact tables (> 2 GB) that participate in frequent JOINs.
Replicated: Stores an entire copy of the table on each compute node; ideal for small dimension tables (< 2 GB) to enable local JOINs without data shuffle.
Round-Robin (default): Distributes rows evenly in a circular fashion without a key; ideal for temporary staging tables during initial data loads.
theoryPill.examTrap: Quick exam rule: Large Fact table -> Hash; Small Dimension table -> Replicated; Staging table (fast ingestion) -> Round-Robin.

questions.domain: Describe an analytics workload on Azure
questions.topic: Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) in a Lakehouse
questions.stem: When designing a Lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric or Azure Databricks following the Medallion architecture (multi-layer data quality framework), data flows through three progressive layers: Bronze, Silver, and Gold. What is the designated purpose of each of these three layers in order?

options.text: Bronze stores raw source data; Silver contains cleaned, conformed, and validated data; and Gold delivers aggregated star-schema data ready for Power BI reporting.
options.rationale: Correct. The Medallion architecture structures progressive refinement: Bronze (Raw ingestion) -> Silver (Cleaned/Validated/Conformed) -> Gold (Curated/Aggregated/Business-ready).

options.text: Bronze stores final curated Power BI semantic models; Silver preserves archive backups; and Gold retains unvalidated raw streaming events without schema enforcement.
options.rationale: Incorrect. This completely reverses the progressive data refinement flow of the Medallion architecture.

options.text: Bronze, Silver, and Gold represent global replication consistency levels configurable within an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL account container.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The five consistency levels in Cosmos DB are Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session, Consistent Prefix, and Eventual.

options.text: Bronze, Silver, and Gold specify the three binary large object blob types (Block, Append, and Page) supported inside Azure Blob Storage accounts.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The three Azure Blob types are Block Blobs, Append Blobs, and Page Blobs.

questions.explanation: The Medallion architecture is the standard design pattern in Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks for logically organizing data in a Lakehouse using Delta Lake tables. As data progresses from Bronze (raw, immutable copy of source data) to Silver (filtered, cleaned, deduplicated, and conformed entities) and finally to Gold (business-level aggregates and dimensional models), its quality, reliability, and analytical readiness increase.

theoryPill.title: The Three Layers of the Medallion Architecture: Bronze, Silver, and Gold
theoryPill.summary: This foundational data engineering pattern is tested across both Azure Databricks and Microsoft Fabric questions in Domain 4 of DP-900.
keyPoints: Bronze Layer (Raw): Exact ingestion of source systems in original format or raw Delta; serves as an immutable historical record.
Silver Layer (Cleaned & Conformed): Deduplicated, schema-validated, cleaned, and standardized business entities.
Gold Layer (Curated & Business-level): Star-schema dimensional modeling (facts and dimensions) and pre-aggregated metrics optimized for Power BI and Direct Lake.
theoryPill.examTrap: Remember the alignment: Bronze = Raw; Silver = Cleaned/Conformed; Gold = Curated/Business-ready for reporting.

questions.domain: Describe an analytics workload on Azure
questions.topic: Lakehouse vs Data Warehouse in Microsoft Fabric
questions.stem: In Microsoft Fabric, both the Lakehouse and the Data Warehouse store tables internally in the open Delta Parquet format on OneLake. However, they target different user personas and developer experiences. Which TWO statements accurately distinguish a Lakehouse from a Data Warehouse in Microsoft Fabric? (Choose two).

options.text: A Lakehouse organizes unstructured Files and Delta Tables, utilizing Apache Spark (PySpark, Scala, Spark SQL) as its primary engine with a read-only SQL endpoint.
options.rationale: Correct. A Fabric Lakehouse is designed for data engineers working with Spark across diverse files and Delta tables, providing a read-only SQL analytics endpoint to query tables with T-SQL.

options.text: A Data Warehouse in Fabric provides a full transactional relational engine supporting complete read and write operations via T-SQL (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and ACID transactions).
options.rationale: Correct. Unlike the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint (which is read-only for tables), the Fabric Data Warehouse offers full DDL/DML write support and enterprise transactions entirely through T-SQL.

options.text: A Data Warehouse in Microsoft Fabric disables all T-SQL queries and requires developers to write data updates using Gremlin graph traversal language exclusively.
options.rationale: Incorrect. T-SQL is the core, native language for all querying and data manipulation inside the Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse.

options.text: A Lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric uses a proprietary binary format that strictly prevents connecting Power BI semantic models or interactive reporting visuals.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Both Lakehouses and Data Warehouses in Fabric natively integrate with Power BI, including ultra-fast Direct Lake mode over OneLake.

options.text: To combine tables between a Lakehouse and a Data Warehouse in the same workspace, all data must first be exported to an external Azure Table Storage account.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Both reside in OneLake in Delta Parquet format and can be joined seamlessly using cross-database T-SQL queries or OneLake shortcuts without data copying.

questions.explanation: In Microsoft Fabric, all analytics engines share OneLake and store structured tables as open Delta Parquet files. The distinction lies in development approach: the Lakehouse is tailored for Spark data engineering (with files and tables, plus a read-only SQL endpoint), whereas the Data Warehouse is built for SQL professionals requiring full T-SQL DDL/DML write capabilities, stored procedures, and multi-table ACID transactions.

theoryPill.title: Choosing Between Lakehouse and Data Warehouse in Microsoft Fabric
theoryPill.summary: Both store Delta tables in OneLake, but differ in their primary development language and write engine (Spark vs full T-SQL).
keyPoints: Fabric Lakehouse: Houses Files (any format) and Tables (Delta); primary write path via Apache Spark, Dataflows, or Pipelines; includes read-only SQL analytics endpoint.
Fabric Data Warehouse: 100% T-SQL read/write experience (CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, multi-table ACID transactions); ideal for teams with SQL Server / Synapse backgrounds.
Interoperability: Cross-database T-SQL queries can join tables between a Data Warehouse and a Lakehouse SQL endpoint without moving data.
theoryPill.examTrap: If a team prefers working with Python/PySpark, notebooks, and unstructured files alongside tables, select Lakehouse; if the team requires full T-SQL write operations and multi-table ACID transactions, select Data Warehouse.

questions.domain: Describe an analytics workload on Azure
questions.topic: Power BI Semantic Model Storage Modes (Import, DirectQuery, Dual)
questions.stem: When connecting Power BI Desktop to relational or analytical data sources, an analyst can configure table storage modes as Import, DirectQuery, or Dual (composite model). Which TWO statements accurately describe the differences between Import mode and DirectQuery mode? (Choose two).

options.text: Import mode loads and compresses data into the Power BI in-memory engine (VertiPaq), delivering maximum interactive speed but requiring scheduled refreshes.
options.rationale: Correct. Import mode is the default and fastest mode because queries run against compressed in-memory columnar cache, but data is only as fresh as the latest scheduled refresh.

options.text: DirectQuery mode leaves data in the underlying source system and translates visual interactions into live queries, ideal for massive volumes or real-time data.
options.rationale: Correct. With DirectQuery, data remains in the source database, and Power BI sends queries on demand whenever reports are opened or filtered.

options.text: DirectQuery mode operates completely offline without network connectivity by bundling an uncompressed copy of all source tables in the local .pbix file.
options.rationale: Incorrect. DirectQuery depends entirely on active network connectivity to the source system to answer every visual query.

options.text: Import mode completely disables DAX measures and prohibits combining tables originating from local files with Azure SQL cloud databases.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Import mode supports the complete range of DAX functions and allows mashups across any combination of supported data sources.

options.text: Dual storage mode converts all semantic model tables into schemaless text files and permanently disables cross-filtering relationships in reports.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Dual mode allows a table (typically a shared dimension) to act as either Import or DirectQuery dynamically depending on the other tables in each query.

questions.explanation: Power BI supports three primary table storage modes: 1) Import (caches data in memory using the high-performance VertiPaq engine; fastest query speeds, full DAX support, requires scheduled refresh); 2) DirectQuery (data remains in source; queries pushed down in real time, ideal for multi-terabyte data or real-time changes); and 3) Dual (acts as either cached Import or pass-through DirectQuery dynamically within composite models).

theoryPill.title: Storage Modes in Power BI: Import vs DirectQuery vs Dual
theoryPill.summary: Selecting the right storage mode balances data freshness, dataset size limitations, and visual query performance.
keyPoints: Import (default): Caches data in memory; delivers blazing query speeds; requires scheduled refresh to show updated records.
DirectQuery: Leaves data in source system; queries translated on demand; supports live data changes and massive datasets.
Dual (Composite models): Can act as either Import or DirectQuery depending on query context to avoid network data movement.
Direct Lake (Microsoft Fabric): Reads Delta Parquet files directly from OneLake into memory without import or slow query translation.
theoryPill.examTrap: If a question requires 'data must never leave the on-premises database due to data residency policies, or the dataset is 30 TB and requires real-time updates', select DirectQuery.

Next, they need to drag relationships between tables to define one-to-many (1:*) relationships in a star schema. Which two tools or views in Power BI Desktop are used respectively for these two tasks?

options.text: Power Query Editor to clean and transform columns, and Model view to configure relationship diagrams.

questions.topic: Selecting Visual Types in Power BI (Scatter, Treemap, Matrix, KPI)
questions.stem:
A data analyst is designing an interactive report in Power BI Desktop and must choose the most appropriate visual for two distinct business scenarios:
1. Compare the relationship and statistical correlation between two continuous numeric measures ('Advertising Spend' on the X-axis and 'Units Sold' on the Y-axis) for each store, using a third measure ('Total Profit') to determine bubble size and spot outliers.
2. Display large volumes of hierarchical data (Product Category -> Subcategory) as a nested set of colored rectangles proportional to sales within the total available canvas space.

Which TWO Power BI visuals should be selected respectively? (Choose two).

options.text: Scatter chart (or Bubble chart) to analyze numerical correlation, clusters, and statistical outliers.
options.rationale: Correct. A Scatter chart (and Bubble chart when adding a measure to the Size field) plots two or three continuous measures across X and Y axes to reveal correlations and identify outliers.

options.text: Treemap to represent hierarchical category proportions as a nested set of colored rectangle tiles.
options.rationale: Correct. A Treemap displays hierarchical data as nested rectangles where each rectangle's area is directly proportional to the measured quantitative value.

options.text: Single number Card visual to display statistical correlations across 500 store locations simultaneously.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A Card visual displays a single aggregate number or KPI metric; it cannot plot dual-axis correlation or category breakdowns.

options.text: Slicer control visual to render nested proportional colored rectangles for hierarchical sales revenues.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A Slicer is an interactive filter control on the canvas used to filter other charts on the page.

options.text: Radial Gauge visual to drill down through four deep hierarchical tiers of product categories.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A Gauge visual shows the progress of a single metric toward a specified target value along a circular arc.

questions.explanation: Exam DP-900 tests selecting the right visual for specific analytical goals: 1) Scatter/Bubble chart (compares two or three continuous numeric measures to uncover correlations and outliers); 2) Treemap (displays hierarchical data as nested rectangles proportional to quantitative values); 3) Matrix (unlike a flat Table, provides row and column grouping with hierarchical drill-down and subtotals); 4) KPI / Gauge (evaluates current metric progress toward a target goal); and 5) Waterfall chart (visualizes sequential increases and decreases leading to a total).

theoryPill.title: Key Visualization Types in Power BI for Exam DP-900

KPI and Gauge: Measure current performance of a single metric against a defined target goal.

questions.domain: Describe considerations for working with non-relational data on Azure
questions.topic: Azure Cosmos DB Consistency Levels
questions.stem: Azure Cosmos DB provides five well-defined consistency levels to balance data consistency against throughput (RU/s) and latency. An e-commerce application requires that whenever a user adds an item to their shopping cart, they immediately see that item reflected in their subsequent read queries, without imposing a global lock across all worldwide read replicas. Which default and most widely adopted consistency level guarantees this behavior?

options.text: Session consistency (default level).
options.rationale: Correct. Session consistency is the default level in Azure Cosmos DB. It guarantees monotonic reads and read-your-own-writes semantics within a client session using a session token, providing optimal performance at the standard cost of 1 RU per 1 KB read.

options.text: Strong consistency (global linearizability).
options.rationale: Incorrect. Strong consistency guarantees immediate global linearizability, but it doubles RU read costs, increases latency, and cannot span across multi-region write accounts.

options.text: Eventual consistency (weakest ordering).
options.rationale: Incorrect. Eventual consistency is the weakest level; it does not guarantee that a client will immediately see its own recent writes.

options.text: Consistent Prefix consistency (in-order updates).
options.rationale: Incorrect. Consistent Prefix ensures that reads never observe out-of-order updates, but it does not guarantee immediate read-your-own-writes visibility within the same session.

questions.explanation: Azure Cosmos DB offers five consistency levels: Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session (default), Consistent Prefix, and Eventual. Session consistency ensures that a client application session always reads its own writes (read-your-own-writes), providing the optimal balance of consistency, latency, and standard 1 RU read cost.

theoryPill.title: The Five Consistency Levels in Azure Cosmos DB
theoryPill.summary: Balancing consistency, availability, latency, and throughput in globally distributed NoSQL data.
keyPoints: Strong: Highest consistency, highest latency, double RU read cost; guarantees globally linearizable reads.
Bounded Staleness: Reads lag behind writes by at most K versions or T time intervals.
Session (Default): Guarantees read-your-own-writes and monotonic reads within a client session; ideal for user profiles and shopping carts.
Consistent Prefix: Ensures updates are never seen out of order.
Eventual: Weakest consistency, lowest latency, lowest RU cost; no order guarantee across replicas.
theoryPill.examTrap: Remember that Session is the default consistency level in Cosmos DB and offers the best performance/consistency balance for web and mobile applications.

options.text: Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin graph traversal API.

questions.topic: Batch vs Streaming Data Ingestion
questions.stem: What is the fundamental difference between batch data processing and streaming data processing?

options.text: Batch processing processes large volumes of accumulated data at scheduled intervals, whereas streaming processes data continuously in real time as events occur.
options.rationale: Correct. Batch processing operates on bounded, static datasets at scheduled intervals (e.g. nightly or monthly). Streaming data processing operates on unbounded continuous streams of data in real time with sub-second or second latencies.

options.text: Batch processing operates exclusively on NoSQL document databases, whereas streaming processing only supports normalized third-normal-form relational tables.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Both batch and stream processing can ingest, transform, and output to both relational and non-relational data stores.

options.text: Streaming processing requires storing all incoming telemetry events in the Azure Blob Storage Archive tier before executing tumbling window aggregations.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Streaming systems ingest and process data in-flight through low-latency brokers such as Azure Event Hubs or IoT Hub, not offline archive storage.

options.text: Both processing models share an identical delayed execution engine and differ only in the Microsoft Entra ID authentication identity provider configured.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Batch and streaming differ fundamentally in data boundedness, processing frequency, latency expectations, and compute engine architectures.

questions.explanation: Batch processing operates on collected, bounded sets of data over scheduled intervals, whereas streaming data processing ingests, processes, and analyzes unbounded data streams continuously as events happen.

theoryPill.title: Batch Processing vs Streaming Data Processing
theoryPill.summary: Core foundational data architectural concepts tested in Exam DP-900.
keyPoints: Batch Processing: Bounded data, higher acceptable latency, bulk computational efficiency (e.g., payroll calculations, monthly financial reporting).
Stream Processing: Unbounded data in motion, low latency required (e.g., credit card fraud detection, medical telemetry, IoT alerts).
Azure Streaming Ingestion: Azure Event Hubs, Azure IoT Hub, Fabric Eventstreams.
Azure Batch Orchestration: Azure Data Factory, Fabric Data Pipelines.
theoryPill.examTrap: If a scenario describes data being analyzed 'as it arrives' or requiring 'immediate alerts with minimal latency', identify it as Stream processing.

questions.domain: Describe an analytics workload on Azure
questions.topic: Parquet Columnar Format in Data Lakes
questions.stem: In an analytical Data Lake on Azure, storing data in Apache Parquet format is strongly recommended over row-oriented text formats such as CSV or JSON. What is the primary technical advantage of Parquet format for analytical (OLAP) workloads?

options.text: Parquet is a compressed columnar format that allows queries to read only the columns required (column projection), drastically reducing disk I/O.
options.rationale: Correct. Apache Parquet organizes data by columns rather than rows. Analytical queries that aggregate a few columns across millions of rows read only referenced columns, benefiting from high data compression and min/max row-group statistics.

options.text: Parquet stores records as human-readable comma-delimited row text, allowing direct manual edits in basic desktop text editors like Notepad.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Parquet is a binary columnar format; human-readable comma-delimited row storage describes CSV files.

options.text: Parquet encrypts and executes row-by-row OLTP transactions with pessimistic locks without requiring an analytical engine like Apache Spark.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Parquet is a columnar file storage format for analytics, not an OLTP database transaction manager with row locking.

options.text: Parquet automatically unzips data into normalized Third Normal Form tables inside Azure Queue Storage message queues to accelerate reports.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Parquet is a data lake file format and has no relation to message queues in Azure Queue Storage.

questions.explanation: The columnar structure of Apache Parquet optimizes query performance and reduces cloud storage and egress costs in modern data lakes such as Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 and OneLake by reading only necessary columns and applying high compression.

theoryPill.title: Columnar Storage: Apache Parquet vs CSV and JSON
theoryPill.summary: The de facto standard format for modern big data analytics in Azure and Microsoft Fabric.
keyPoints: Columnar organization: Stores values of the same column contiguously on disk.
High compression: Identical data types and domains compress with superior ratios (Snappy, GZIP, dictionary encoding).
Column Pruning: If a query requests only 2 of 100 columns, the engine scans only 2% of the file data.
Data Skipping: Embedded statistics (min/max values per row group) allow the query engine to bypass irrelevant row blocks entirely.
theoryPill.examTrap: CSV and JSON are row-oriented formats best suited for data exchange and transactions (OLTP); Parquet is the industry standard for analytical query processing (OLAP).

questions.domain: Describe considerations for working with non-relational data on Azure
questions.topic: Azure Cosmos DB Partition Keys
questions.stem: You are designing an Azure Cosmos DB container to store millions of customer transaction documents. To ensure horizontal scalability without performance bottlenecks and prevent 'hot partitions' from exhausting provisioned Request Units (RU/s), what is the primary criterion for selecting an effective Partition Key?

options.text: Choose a property with high cardinality that evenly distributes both RU/s throughput consumption and data storage volume across logical partitions.
options.rationale: Correct. A well-designed partition key in Cosmos DB must evenly distribute storage and throughput across logical partitions. Choosing an attribute with a wide range of distinct values (high cardinality) prevents hot partition bottlenecks.

options.text: Choose a boolean flag property with only two potential values (true or false) to concentrate all transaction writes into two physical partitions.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A boolean attribute with only two distinct values restricts data to just two logical partitions, creating immediate hot partitions.

options.text: Choose an optional attribute containing a null value in 99% of documents to group customer transactions inside a single partition boundary.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Storing 99% of transactions under a null partition key concentrates nearly all traffic on one partition, causing throttling.

options.text: Define a static partition key with an identical constant string for all customers and dynamically redefine it during every SELECT query executed.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Partition keys are immutable once a container is created, and using a constant value concentrates all operations onto one partition.

questions.explanation: Selecting an effective partition key is the most critical design decision in Azure Cosmos DB. A hot partition occurs when one partition receives significantly more traffic or storage than others, exhausting its allocated throughput and triggering HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) throttling.

theoryPill.title: Partition Key Selection Strategy in Azure Cosmos DB
theoryPill.summary: Achieving horizontal scale and preventing hot partitions in distributed NoSQL databases.
keyPoints: High cardinality: Must possess thousands or millions of possible distinct values (e.g., UserId, DeviceId, OrderId).
Even distribution: Storage footprint and read/write request volumes must be spread uniformly across partitions.
Query efficiency: Including the partition key in query WHERE filters routes requests directly to a single partition.
Physical limit: A single logical partition can hold a maximum of 20 GB of data.
theoryPill.examTrap: Never select low-cardinality attributes (such as Gender, Marital Status, or Year) as partition keys; they inevitably cause hot partitions.

questions.topic: Data Factory Pipelines: Copy Activity vs Mapping Data Flows
questions.stem: In Azure Data Factory (and Fabric Data Pipelines), you need to transfer raw, untransformed data from an on-premises SFTP server to Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 as fast as possible with the lowest compute cost. Which built-in pipeline activity should you use?

options.text: Copy Activity for high-throughput, low-cost direct data ingestion.
options.rationale: Correct. Copy Activity is the most performant and cost-effective native mechanism for data movement (ELT). It connects to over 100 supported sources and sinks without spinning up Spark clusters for in-memory transformations.

options.text: Mapping Data Flow executing on an on-demand Apache Spark cluster.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Mapping Data Flows spin up Apache Spark clusters for in-memory data transformations, adding cluster spin-up latency and unnecessary cost for simple file copy operations.

options.text: Web Activity making individual REST HTTP calls per transferred record.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Web Activity is intended for invoking web endpoints or webhook callbacks, not for bulk file transfers.

options.text: Wait Activity pausing pipeline execution for an arbitrary time delay.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Wait Activity merely delays pipeline execution without performing any data movement.

questions.explanation: Copy Activity is the core data movement engine in Azure Data Factory. For straightforward extraction and ingestion (ELT) without complex in-flight transformations, Copy Activity delivers the highest throughput at the lowest operational cost.

questions.stem: Your company has thousands of Parquet and CSV files stored in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2. options.text: Serverless SQL pool.
options.rationale: Correct. Azure Synapse serverless SQL pool enables querying data directly in Azure Data Lake Storage (using OPENROWSET or external views) with T-SQL, requiring no dedicated infrastructure and billing per terabyte processed.

options.text: Dedicated SQL pool.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A dedicated SQL pool requires provisioning fixed Data Warehouse Units (DWUs) billed per hour regardless of how many queries are executed.

options.text: Synapse Spark pool.

questions.topic: Azure Blob Storage Access Tiers
questions.stem: A legal department must preserve signed contract copies for 10 years to comply with regulatory requirements. These documents are rarely accessed (less than once per year). In the event of an audit, a retrieval delay of several hours to rehydrate and download the files is acceptable. The company requires the lowest possible storage cost per gigabyte. Which Azure Blob Storage access tier should you select?

options.text: Archive access tier.
options.rationale: Correct. The Archive tier offers the lowest storage cost per gigabyte for data at rest. Blobs remain offline and require a rehydration process that can take up to 15 hours with standard priority.

options.text: Hot online access tier.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The Hot tier has the highest storage cost per gigabyte and the lowest access cost; it is intended for frequently accessed daily data.

options.text: Cool online access tier.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The Cool tier is optimized for data that will remain stored for at least 30 days and accessed infrequently (such as once per month).

options.text: Cold online access tier.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The Cold tier is an online tier intermediate between Cool and Archive (requiring a 90-day minimum retention), but it costs more per gigabyte than Archive.

questions.explanation: The Archive tier in Azure Blob Storage provides the lowest storage costs for long-term historical records that can tolerate a retrieval latency of several hours.

theoryPill.title: Azure Blob Storage Access Tiers (Hot, Cool, Cold, Archive)
theoryPill.summary: Cost optimization based on data access frequency.

Cool: Lower storage cost, higher access cost. Minimum retention period of 30 days.
Cold: Storage cost between Cool and Archive. Minimum retention period of 90 days.
Archive: Lowest storage cost, highest read cost. Data is stored offline and requires rehydration (several hours).

questions.domain: Describe considerations for working with non-relational data on Azure
questions.topic: Azure Cosmos DB Consistency Levels
questions.stem: When working with Azure Cosmos DB, you must choose from five configurable consistency levels. Which consistency level is the default setting that guarantees read-your-own-writes semantics for an individual client session, providing an optimal balance of throughput, availability, and latency?

options.text: Session consistency.
options.rationale: Correct. Session consistency is the default level in Azure Cosmos DB. It guarantees monotonic reads, monotonic writes, and read-your-own-writes within the client session, making it ideal for web and mobile apps.

options.text: Strong consistency.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Strong consistency guarantees linearizability (reads always return the most recent committed write), but it incurs higher latency and cannot span multiple Azure regions with multi-region writes.

options.text: Eventual consistency.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Eventual consistency offers the lowest latency and highest throughput, but it provides no ordering guarantees or immediate read-your-own-writes guarantees.

options.text: Bounded staleness.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Bounded staleness guarantees that reads lag behind writes by at most K versions or T time intervals, but it is not the default consistency level.

questions.explanation: Session consistency is the default and most widely used consistency level in Azure Cosmos DB, offering read-your-own-writes guarantees for a user session without the latency overhead of Strong consistency.

theoryPill.title: Five Consistency Levels in Azure Cosmos DB
theoryPill.summary: Trade-offs between consistency, availability, and latency (CAP theorem).
keyPoints: 1. Strong: Linearizability; reads always return the latest version. Highest latency.
2. Bounded Staleness: Reads lag behind writes by at most K versions or T time window.
3. Session (Default): Guarantees read-your-own-writes within the client session context.
4. Consistent Prefix: Updates are never seen out of order, but updates may lag behind.
5. Eventual: Weakest consistency; lowest latency, highest availability, out-of-order reads possible until convergence.
theoryPill.examTrap: Default consistency level for Azure Cosmos DB? It is always 'Session'.
theoryPill.searchQuery: Azure Cosmos DB five consistency levels session DP-900

options.text: Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB (HTAP analytical store).

options.text: A scheduled Azure Data Factory batch pipeline executing hourly.

options.text: A direct cross-partition query against the OLTP container.

options.text: Scaling up the provisioned RU/s on the transactional container.

questions.topic: Batch Processing vs Streaming Data Processing
questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes a key difference between batch processing and streaming (real-time) data processing?

options.text: Batch processing collects and processes large volumes of data at scheduled intervals, whereas stream processing analyzes continuous events in real time as they arrive.
options.rationale: Correct. Batch processing operates on stored data at scheduled intervals (such as nightly runs), whereas stream processing continuously ingests and evaluates unbounded data streams with second or sub-second latency.

options.text: Stream processing can only ingest normalized relational tables, whereas batch processing operates exclusively on unformatted plain text files.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Both batch and streaming paradigms can process structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data types.

options.text: Batch processing requires a mandatory minimum interval of seven days between executions and cannot be automated using event-driven triggers.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Batch jobs can be scheduled at any interval (minutes, hours, or daily) and can be triggered by automated schedules or event-driven triggers.

options.text: Stream processing cannot calculate mathematical aggregations such as moving averages (`AVG`) or sums (`SUM`) across continuous time windows.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Stream processing engines natively compute aggregations over continuous time windows (tumbling, hopping, and sliding windows).

questions.explanation: Batch processing handles large volumes of historical data at periodic intervals, whereas streaming data processing evaluates data streams continuously in real time as events occur.

theoryPill.title: Batch Processing vs Stream Processing
theoryPill.summary: Core data processing concepts in Azure.
keyPoints: Batch: Historical data at rest, high volume, tolerable latency (minutes to hours), scheduled or event-driven.
Streaming: Data in motion, low latency (milliseconds to seconds), continuous event streams evaluated over time windows.
Azure services for Batch: Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Spark, Fabric Data Pipelines.
Azure services for Streaming: Azure Event Hubs, Azure Stream Analytics, Fabric Real-Time Intelligence.
theoryPill.examTrap: When the scenario requires 'immediate analysis of continuous events as they occur', choose streaming rather than batch processing.

questions.topic: Relational Database Normalization
questions.stem: What is the primary objective of normalization in relational database management system (RDBMS) design?

options.text: Reduce data redundancy, prevent insertion, update, and deletion anomalies, and enforce relational referential integrity.
options.rationale: Correct. Database normalization decomposes complex tables into smaller, well-structured related tables using primary and foreign keys to eliminate unnecessary duplication and prevent update anomalies.

options.text: Consolidate all business entities into a single denormalized table with 500 columns to eliminate relational `JOIN` operations.
options.rationale: Incorrect. This describes denormalization, which is often used in analytical data warehouses but is the exact opposite of relational normalization.

options.text: Convert all relational database tables into schemaless JSON document collections stored within Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Normalization is a relational design technique formulated for relational tables and relational schemas, not NoSQL document stores.

options.text: Remove all primary key (`PRIMARY KEY`) and foreign key (`FOREIGN KEY`) constraints to maximize query execution speeds.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Primary and foreign keys are essential components of normalized relational database schemas to maintain data integrity.

questions.explanation: Relational normalization structures data to minimize redundancy and prevent transactional anomalies, ensuring data integrity across related tables.

theoryPill.title: Data Normalization vs Denormalization
theoryPill.summary: Transactional relational design (OLTP) versus analytical design (OLAP).
keyPoints: Normalization (OLTP): Multiple related tables, eliminates redundancy, optimizes write performance and data integrity (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE).
Normal forms: 1NF (atomic values), 2NF (full functional dependency), 3NF (no transitive dependencies).
Denormalization (OLAP / Data Warehouse): Fewer tables, controlled duplication, optimizes large read queries and aggregations by avoiding expensive JOINs.
theoryPill.examTrap: OLTP favors normalization (integrity and write efficiency); analytical data warehouses / OLAP favor denormalization (star schema).
theoryPill.searchQuery: Database normalization concepts relational DP-900

references.title: Relational data concepts - Microsoft Learn | DP-900

questions.domain: Describe an analytics workload on Azure
questions.topic: Star Schema: Fact Tables vs Dimension Tables
questions.stem: In a star schema dimensional model for a data warehouse, what is the primary role of a dimension table?

options.text: Provide descriptive context (such as customer, product, store, or date) to filter, group, and slice business metrics.
options.rationale: Correct. Dimension tables contain qualitative descriptive attributes (who, what, where, when) used to slice, dice, and filter numeric metrics found in fact tables.

options.text: Store exclusively quantitative numeric measurements and transaction amounts (such as total sales revenue and units sold).
options.rationale: Incorrect. This describes a fact table, which holds numeric measures, rather than a dimension table.

options.text: Record operating system audit traces and low-level network packets for Azure SQL Database virtual machines.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Dimension tables model business attributes in analytical models, not operational infrastructure logs or network traces.

options.text: Replace Azure role-based access control (RBAC) security assignments and network firewall rules in the data warehouse.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Dimension tables are schema elements in a data warehouse model; they do not configure cloud network or identity security.

questions.explanation: In a star schema, dimension tables provide descriptive attributes to slice and filter data, whereas fact tables store numeric measurements and foreign keys.

theoryPill.title: Star Schema: Facts and Dimensions
theoryPill.summary: Standard dimensional modeling structure for data warehouses and Power BI.
keyPoints: Fact table: Contains additive numeric measurements (sales amounts, quantities, costs) and foreign keys referencing dimension tables.
Dimension table: Contains descriptive business attributes (customer name, product category, store location, calendar date).
Star schema: A central fact table connected to multiple surrounding dimension tables via one-to-many relationships.

questions.domain: Describe considerations for working with non-relational data on Azure
questions.topic: Azure Cosmos DB Partition Key Selection
questions.stem: You are designing an Azure Cosmos DB container for a package tracking application that will process millions of reads and writes daily. To ensure uniform storage and Request Unit (RU) distribution and prevent hot partitions, which characteristic must an effective partition key possess?

options.text: Have high cardinality (many distinct values) and evenly distribute read/write requests and storage.
options.rationale: Correct. A good partition key in Azure Cosmos DB must have high cardinality (such as deviceId, trackingId, or customerId) and distribute storage and request volume evenly across physical partitions without bottlenecks.

options.text: Have only two distinct values (such as `'Active'` and `'Inactive'`) to concentrate all records.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A low-cardinality key causes hot partitions that quickly breach the 20 GB logical partition storage limit and throttle throughput.

options.text: Contain a static numeric constant such as `0` across all documents inserted into the container.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Using a static constant forces all items into a single physical partition, defeating the purpose of horizontal scaling.

options.text: Dynamically change the property name used as the partition key on every query executed by clients.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The partition key path is defined when the container is created and cannot be altered per query.

questions.explanation: An optimal partition key in Azure Cosmos DB must have high cardinality and distribute read and write throughput evenly to avoid creating hot partitions.

theoryPill.title: Partition Key Design in Azure Cosmos DB
theoryPill.summary: Core strategy for horizontal scalability and partition balance.
keyPoints: Logical partition: Items sharing the same partition key value (limited to 20 GB storage per logical partition).
Physical partition: Internal compute and SSD storage resources managed automatically by Azure.
Good key criteria: High cardinality, uniform request distribution across time, frequently used in query filters.
Avoid: Low cardinality keys (e.g., status flags) or keys that create hot partitions (e.g., current date where all writes hit one partition).
theoryPill.examTrap: 'Hot partitions' are prevented by choosing partition keys with HIGH CARDINALITY and uniform access patterns.
theoryPill.searchQuery: Partitioning and horizontal scaling in Azure Cosmos DB DP-900

references.title: Partitioning and horizontal scaling in Azure Cosmos DB | Microsoft Learn

questions.topic: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 Hierarchical Namespace
questions.stem: Which core feature distinguishes Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 from standard Azure Blob Storage, enabling atomic directory operations (such as renaming or moving multi-petabyte folders instantly without copying files one by one)?

options.text: Hierarchical namespace (HNS).
options.rationale: Correct. The hierarchical namespace organizes objects into a true directory hierarchy (POSIX-like), allowing atomic directory renames and moves that drastically improve performance for big data engines like Apache Spark.

options.text: Unencrypted FTP network protocol.
options.rationale: Incorrect. ADLS Gen2 uses the ABFS (Azure Blob File System) driver over HTTPS optimized for analytics, not unencrypted legacy FTP.

options.text: Restriction to JPEG image files.
options.rationale: Incorrect. ADLS Gen2 supports all file types (Parquet, Delta, CSV, JSON, ORC, binary, text, etc.).

options.text: A 10-megabyte total storage limit.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Azure storage accounts can store multiple petabytes of data, not just 10 megabytes.

questions.explanation: The Hierarchical Namespace (HNS) is the defining feature of Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, enabling true directories, POSIX ACLs, and atomic metadata operations.

theoryPill.title: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 and Hierarchical Namespace (HNS)
theoryPill.summary: Object storage optimized for big data analytics engines.
keyPoints: Standard Blob Storage: Flat namespace where 'directories' are simulated prefixes. Renaming a directory requires copying every blob individually.
ADLS Gen2 with HNS: Real directory hierarchy. Renaming a 10 TB directory is an instantaneous atomic metadata operation.
Security: Supports granular POSIX-compliant Access Control Lists (ACLs) on files and folders in addition to Azure RBAC.
ABFS driver: High-throughput driver optimized for Apache Spark, Hadoop, and Databricks.
theoryPill.examTrap: The fundamental difference between Blob Storage and ADLS Gen2 is the 'Hierarchical Namespace' (HNS).

questions.topic: Query Folding
questions.stem: You are developing a Power BI Desktop report connected to an Azure SQL Database using Import storage mode. In Power Query Editor, you apply several transformation steps: filtering by fiscal year, removing 15 unnecessary columns, and changing data types on 3 numeric columns. You want to ensure that the relational source database engine executes these operations rather than processing them locally in the Power Query mashup engine. Which Power Query concept describes this capability, and how can you verify whether it is functioning?

options.text: Query folding; right-click the last applied transformation step and verify that the 'View Native Query' option is enabled.
options.rationale: Correct. Query folding translates Power Query M transformations into a single SQL query executed directly on the source relational engine. It is verified using the 'View Native Query' option.

options.text: Table buffering (Table.Buffer); inspect the local Resource Monitor to verify memory allocation for the Microsoft.Mashup.Container process.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Table.Buffer loads table data into local client memory and breaks query folding back to the relational source.

options.text: Direct Lake analytic processing; review the session diagnostics telemetry log located within Power BI Desktop advanced diagnostic settings.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Direct Lake is an exclusive storage mode for semantic models in Microsoft Fabric on OneLake (Delta Parquet format), not an Azure SQL connection in Power BI Desktop.

options.text: Incremental refresh partitioning; verify that the 'Enable Load' property is selected in the context menu of the Power Query M query.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Enable load specifies whether the table is exposed to the Power BI Desktop data model, not whether transformations fold back to the source.

questions.explanation: Query folding is the ability of Power Query to translate M transformation steps into a native SQL query sent directly to the relational data source. When 'View Native Query' is available and active, the Azure SQL database performs the filtering and column projection, conserving network bandwidth and local machine memory.

theoryPill.title: Query Folding in Power Query
theoryPill.summary: Query folding optimizes data ingestion by delegating filtering, aggregation, and joins to the underlying relational database engine, minimizing data transfer.
keyPoints: Enables incremental refresh to operate efficiently through date partition filters.
Verified by right-clicking an applied step and selecting 'View Native Query'.
Steps such as complex custom M functions, arbitrary type conversions, or cross-source merges break query folding.
theoryPill.examTrap: When a transformation step breaks query folding, all subsequent steps are evaluated locally by the Power Query mashup engine or gateway, downloading millions of unfiltered rows.
theoryPill.searchQuery: Power Query folding View Native Query Microsoft Learn

references.title: Query folding guidance in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn

questions.topic: Storage Modes
questions.stem: Your company has a sales data warehouse containing more than 2 billion rows in an Azure Synapse Analytics dedicated SQL pool, along with small Customer and Product dimension tables (50,000 rows). Executive management requires fast-loading dashboards with aggregated annual metrics, while business analysts require real-time drill-down to individual transactional details without exceeding Power BI Pro memory limits. Which storage mode architecture should you configure?

options.text: Configure a composite model with aggregated summary tables in Import mode, the transactional fact table in DirectQuery mode, and the shared dimensions in Dual mode.
options.rationale: Correct. A composite model with aggregations provides optimal performance: aggregate tables in Import mode ensure instant executive dashboard performance, DirectQuery fact tables handle granular transactional drill-down without exhausting RAM, and Dual mode dimensions dynamically adapt to satisfy both local queries and remote source joins.

options.text: Configure all tables in Import mode using VertiPaq columnar compression and schedule eight daily automated refreshes configured with Power Query date partitions.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Importing 2 billion granular transactions exceeds the 1 GB semantic model size limit in Power BI Pro shared capacity.

options.text: Configure all fact and dimension tables exclusively in DirectQuery mode with report query caching enabled at the shared Power BI Pro workspace capacity level.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Running all fact and dimension queries exclusively in DirectQuery creates significant latency for executive dashboards, generating costly SQL queries on the data warehouse during every interaction.

options.text: Configure a Live Connection to the transactional data warehouse combined with local dimension tables imported from an enterprise OneDrive for Business folder.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Live Connection is supported only against SQL Server Analysis Services, Azure Analysis Services, or existing Power BI semantic models; it cannot connect to raw data warehouses or combine local imported tables into composite models.

questions.explanation: Composite models with aggregations combine the speed of Import mode for summarized reporting with the real-time reach of DirectQuery for granular data. Setting shared dimension tables to Dual mode allows Power BI to query them from in-memory cache when querying Import tables, or join them directly at the source when querying DirectQuery fact tables, preventing cross-source boundary data transfers.

theoryPill.title: Storage Modes: Import, DirectQuery, and Dual
theoryPill.summary: Power BI composite models allow combining multiple storage modes within a single semantic model to optimize query performance and accommodate massive data volumes.
keyPoints: Import: Cached in VertiPaq memory, delivers blazing query speeds, limited by RAM and requires scheduled refreshes.
DirectQuery: Leaves data at the relational source and executes SQL queries in real time upon visual interaction.
Dual: Acts dynamically as either Import or DirectQuery depending on the tables involved in the generated DAX query.
theoryPill.examTrap: If a dimension is set to Import mode while the fact table is DirectQuery, querying them together causes inefficient cross-source queries. The dimension should be set to Dual mode.
theoryPill.searchQuery: composite models storage mode dual import directquery Power BI
